claim: Combining structural uncertainty with answer dispersion (StructU+Self-ConsU) yields highest or second-highest selection AUC on mathematical reasoning and knowledge tasks, with largest gains where answer-level agreement alone is insufficient to identify unreliable reasoning.
falsifier: On a held-out set of mathematical reasoning and knowledge tasks, the combined estimator should achieve higher Sel-AUC than either component alone, with the largest improvements on the hardest instances (e.g., contest-level problems).

conditions: settings where answer-level agreement alone is insufficient
exclusions: limited to the five LLMs and eight benchmarks studied; transfer beyond these systems and tasks is unestablished

title: Combined structural uncertainty for selection AUC for identifying
